about: This Tobey Maguire template is a still from Sam Raimi's Spider-Man films: Peter Parker walks down a busy New York street next to Mary Jane (Kirsten Dunst), who leans in toward the camera mid-sentence with a big smile. Peter, in a dark jacket, looks down and slightly away with a stiff, uncomfortable expression, as if he is trying very hard not to react. The contrast between her chatty enthusiasm and his frozen, swallowed panic is what people caption: it reads as the face you make when someone casually says something alarming and you have to keep walking.
usage:
The top box sets up the moment and the bottom box finishes it, usually something like "when someone says ___" split across both lines. The best captions describe news delivered casually that the listener has a strong private reaction to, so Mary Jane plays the oblivious speaker and Peter plays you.

Work disasters announced in passing, spoilers dropped mid-conversation and awkward social revelations all fit. Keep the setup ordinary and let the bottom line carry the bad news.
